issue.description:
Validate a versioned JSON manifest composed strictly of existing command primitives (creates, updates, labels, dependencies, closes) with local references for newly created IDs; show a dry-run diff; then commit all operations in one transaction that publishes at most one checkpoint generation under R026. v1 must refuse any semantics a single existing command does not already have.

Adopted from the run-1 deferral: per-mutation publication makes N-command materialization N generations, and interrupted materializations still discard entire disposable workspaces.

Acceptance:
- manifest v1 schema specified as thin composition of existing primitives
- dry-run reports the full semantic delta without mutation
- commit is all-or-none in one transaction, one checkpoint generation
- result map links manifest entries to created/updated IDs

Refs: plan section 12 R033; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 6 dossier; run-1 finalist 6.
issue.notes:
Completed in two layers.

Found: the previous run's R033 implementation (src/service/manifest.rs, CLI wiring, bulk-manifests-v1.md spec) had already landed, swept into 154e3d3 by that worker's blanket staging, but was dead on arrival: parse_operation handed serde the operation object still carrying its 'op' key against deny_unknown_fields structs, so every valid manifest failed document validation with 'unknown field op'. The conformance test file was never committed, which is why nobody saw it.

Done (commit 9b5ffd3, pushed):
- Fixed the parser (strip the consumed discriminator before the closed-schema parse) and a clippy lint in manifest.rs.
- Landed tests/r033_bulk_manifests.rs (9 tests) after correcting it against real checkpoint semantics: escaped quotes inside raw-string manifests, an init-appends-events assumption (init writes zero events), a no-op snapshot taken before an intervening close's own publication, and per-command generation turnover observed via distinct generation_id instead of object-file counts (retention deletes superseded roots, so files do not accumulate).
- Repaired three pre-existing red tests the full-suite gate surfaced, all verified on pristine HEAD: docs help coverage (eight hidden R037 near-miss flags lacked help text), cli_lifecycle close-empty-reason (R037 commit changed the message case away from the canonical service-layer wording), and the contract test's manifest entries.
- Regenerated man pages: bead-manifest{,-commit,-dry-run}.1 plus never-generated resource/sync-fork/sync-reconcile pages.

Verified: fmt clean, clippy zero warnings, full suite 55 targets / 868 passing / 6 failing - all six are the pre-existing R028 fork-identity vs R027 reconcile cluster (5x r028_fork_identity events.sequence UNIQUE violations; reconcile's validate_event_sequence rejects fork origins starting at the fork point). Verified identical on pristine HEAD via stash; filed as beadrs-d2e1b26f rather than expanding this bead's scope.

issue.description:
ADR-005 (Accepted 2026-08-16) specifies a doctor check under the `dependencies` scope that warns when open issues carry an assignee — a state excluded from the ready frontier, never claimable, and currently invisible: `bead show` renders it as a healthy open issue and the 2026-08-16 fleet sweep found 583 such issues across 47 of 66 workspaces (ten workspaces fully starved) while doctor reported healthy. The check must be advisory only: warn, name a bounded sample of offending ids, and state the exact remedy `bead update <id> --clear-assignee`; doctor must never clear an assignee, not even under `--repair`. Deliver the check with tests (assigned-open warned, in_progress and unassigned-open not warned, empty-ready-frontier workspace surfaces it, `--repair` leaves assignment untouched), and record the ADR-005 acknowledged follow-up that no marker yet exists for deliberately held assignments.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand

comments.body: Evidence from beadrs-745ef223 (2026-10-25, pre-existing on 43a77715): section 12 scenario 1 ("the old generation remains restorable via previous.json") currently fails on main. On any set-v2 workspace whose open tail has grown since the previous publication, verify_restore_source refuses the retained generation: `bead restore --source .beads/checkpoint --generation <previous.json's gen>` exits 5 with "Unverified restore source: tail set/tail.jsonl unusable: set-v2 artifact set/tail.jsonl is 729 bytes, manifest records 364". Repro: init a workspace, run two mutating commands (two publications below SEG_SEAL), then restore the previous generation. Spec 6.2 lets later publications append to the shared tail, so the retained manifest's tail row can no longer describe the live file by whole-file byte_length; the fix needs either prefix-verified tail reads or seal-on-publication semantics for retained generations. This also blocks archaeology diff/bisect against a live workspace's previous.json (beadrs-745ef223 works against committed/frozen snapshots).
